sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year, from $65.1 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F10][F201].
FY2019 was the trough, with operating margin at 8.1% [F23], down 11.9pp [D109], after a $6.8 billion goodwill impairment [X109].
The filing attributes the Shave Care impairment to currency devaluations, slower grooming category growth and competition [P62][X109].
Operating income rose 186.2% in FY2020 to $15.7 billion [D148][F14], and $8.3 billion of that increase was the base-period impairment charge [P71][X112].
Non-US geographies supplied most of FY2026 growth, rising 6.1% [D510] and adding 3.1pp of the 3.3% total [D511][D457].
Non-US is 52.0% of revenue [D509], while the US share rose from 40.8% in FY2018 [D512] to 47.9% [D534] and US growth slowed to 0.2% [D535].
Beauty was the largest segment contributor, adding 1.3pp on 7.1% growth to $16.0 billion [D603][D602][S45].
The filing attributes FY2026 net sales growth to favourable foreign exchange and pricing, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26][D457].
Diluted EPS rose 1.7% [D461] against net income growth of 0.5% [D459], as the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D476].
Operating margin was 22.7% in FY2026 [F30], above its window median of 22.1% [D648] and below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [D647].
The filing attributes the 1.6pp fall [D470] to lower gross margin and higher marketing spending [P25][D470].
In the FY2026 bridge, cost of revenue took 1.0pp [D483] and SG&A 0.6pp [D485] of the operating margin.
In the largest move, FY2019, other lines took 12.1pp [D125], which the filing ties to the goodwill and intangible impairments [P62][X109].
Operating margin ranks at the 80th percentile of five staples peers [D668], against a peer median of 14.3% [D669].

Net margin of 18.4% [F50] sat 4.3pp below operating margin [F30][F50], as the effective tax rate rose to 20.8% [D443] from 20.3% [D392] on lower share-based compensation benefits and unfavourable geographic mix [P23][D443].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion [F80] was 1.22x net income [D444], and free cash flow of $15.1 billion [F100] was 0.94x [D445], against a window median of 1.02x [D660].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% [D441] is close to its 17.2% window median [D654], while capex of 5.1% of revenue [D440] was 1.40x D&A [D446].

Capex rose 16.9% [D464], driven mainly by capital expenditure and net investment hedge settlements, partly offset by Glad joint venture proceeds [P2][D464]; the filing says working capital added little, with inventory up 8.2% [P3][D480].
Net cash was -$24.2 billion, or -27.8% of revenue [D450][D451], at the 33rd percentile of six staples peers against a median of -1.0% [D676][D677].
That is an improvement of $0.7 billion from -$24.9 billion in FY2025 [D399][D450].
Liquidity is thin: the current ratio is 0.68x [F180] against a window median of 0.72x [D663], with cash of $9.9 billion [F140].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $15.3 billion [D452], 100.7% of FCF [D453], with dividends of $10.2 billion [X144] and buybacks of $5.0 billion [X134], down from $6.5 billion in FY2025 [X133].
Shares fell 1.3% [D476], and return on equity of 30.1% [D456] sits at the 33rd percentile of six peers against a median of 44.4% [D680][D681].

The current ratio is 0.68x [F180] against the candidate threshold below 1.0x [R1], and it sits below 1.0x in every year of the window [F171][F180], with short-term borrowings of $4.8 billion [X204] inside current liabilities of $38.7 billion [F160].
This looks structural rather than new, since cash generation has covered it, but the reliance on short-term funding deserves watching.
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded FCF in FY2025 at 116.6% [R2][D402] and in FY2026 at 100.7% [D453], with dividends rising to $10.2 billion [X144]; the filings cited do not explain the payout rise.
The pattern has persisted for two years, so it reads as a capital allocation choice rather than a one-off, though the filings cited do not say so.
Operating income fell 3.4% [D458] while revenue rose 3.3% [D457], an incremental margin of -25.6% [D481]; the filing attributes the decline to lower gross margin and higher marketing [P25][D481].
Operating margin holding at or above the FY2026 level of 22.7% [F30] would confirm the trend; a return below the 22.1% window median [D648] in the FY2027 10-K would reverse it.
Buybacks plus dividends falling back toward the FY2024 level of 86.6% of FCF [D350], from 100.7% [D453], would confirm the payout is easing, as shown in the FY2027 10-K.
The current ratio staying above the 0.63x window low [D661], from 0.68x [F180], would show liquidity pressure is contained in the FY2027 10-K.
